reason: No cited evidence is provided for any of the key premises. The claims about specific microstructural evolution (nanotwins, dislocation density, oxide scale composition), their dependence on heat treatment temperature, and their effect on wear in FeNiCrCoCu are entirely unsupported by prior results.
premises: Moderate heat treatment (~500 °C) of as-sprayed FeNiCrCoCu induces fine nanotwins and high dislocation density
Moderate heat treatment (~500 °C) forms a thin, adherent, protective Cr/Cu-rich oxide scale
Nanotwins, dislocations, and oxide scale together increase microhardness and reduce high-temperature wear
Higher temperature treatments cause grain coarsening and hardness reduction, worsening wear
As-sprayed coating has coarse grains, low dislocation density, and no protective oxide
